sentences.text:
Hemant Ahirwar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 January,
2025
Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Gwl:365
 1 Mcrc-5142
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Gwalior

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Rajendra Kumar Vani

On The 8 th Of January, 2025
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 51421 of 2024
 Hemant Ahirwar
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Vijay Pratap Singh Tomar - Advocate for the applicant.
 Shri Harish Sharma - Public Prosecutor for the State.
 Order

1. This is the second application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of bail relating to Crime No.44/2024 registered at Police Station Kotwali, District Gwalior (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 363, 366a, 376(2N), 376/115, 376(3), 323, 506 of IPC, Sections 5(L)/6, 3/4,
16/17 of the POCSO Act and Sections 3(1)(w)(i) and 3(2)(v) of the SC/ST Act, 1989.
2.Allegation against the applicant is that he committed rape with the prosecutrix.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that first bail application of the applicant was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 10.09.2024 passed in M.Cr.C.No.37899/2024.
Thereafter the prosecutrix has been examined before the learned trial Court on 11.09.2024, a copy of her statement is appended on record.
In the statement, prosecutrix has admitted NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:365 2 MCRC-51421-2024 that she went with present applicant to visit Delhi.
Other female members were also accompanying them.
It is also admitted by the prosecutrix that she visited Lal Kila in Delhi and at that several persons were present there, but she did not raise any alarm.
Various contradictions and omissions also revealed from her statement which render her statement doubtful.
The entire story of the prosecution qua present applicant appears to be doubtful.
Applicant has no criminal history.
He has been falsely implicated in the case.
He is ready and willing to abide by all the terms and conditions which may be imposed by this Court.
Conclusion of trial will take time.
On these grounds, learned counsel prays for grant of bail to the applicant.
4. Per contra, learned counsel for the State opposed the bail application and prayed to dismiss the bail application.

6. Considering the rival submissions of learned counsel for the parties and attending facts and circumstances of the case, but without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, this application is allowed and it is directed that the applicant be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/-(Rupees One Lac Only) with a solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court/committal Court.
In case, if he is found involved in the offence of same nature, this bail order shall stand cancelled automatically without further reference to the Bench.
Copy of this order be sent to the trial Court concerned for compliance.
